questions.question: Government is focusing on palm tree cultivation to fulfil the need of edible oil & reduce the export burden of palm oil in this region due to its climatic condition and soil favours the palm tree cultivation. This region lies in which agroclimatic zone
questions.explanation: Island zone offers the best climatic condition required for the cultivation of palm tree oil palm is a humid crop. Requires evenly distributed rainfall of 150mm/ month or 2500-4000mm/annum. Rainfall distribution in india is not even and adequate. Hence grow oil palm under assured irrigation conditions by adopting recommended practices. Crop comes up well between 29-33oc max. And 22-24oc min. Temperatures and with bright sunlight for at least 5 hrs. Per day. Humidity of more than 80% is required to come up well[cite: 14].

questions.question: Planning commission classified India into 15 agroclimatic zones on the basis of which of the following parameters: A. Homogeneity of rainfall & temperature B. Difference in topography level C. Similar cropping pattern & cropping system D. Difference in availability of water resources

options.c: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Classification by planning commission of India (1989) made an attempt to delineate the country into different Agro climatic regions based on homogeneity in rainfall, temperature, topography, cropping and farming systems and water resources[cite: 14].

questions.question: Plantation crops like walnut, apricot, almond etc are generally grown in which of the following agroclimatic zones
questions.explanation: Western Himalayan zone-this zone consists of three distinct sub-zones of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh hills. Features: The region consists of skeletal soils of cold region, podzolic mountain meadow soils and hilly brown soils. Lands of the region have steep slopes in undulating terrain. Soils are generally silty loams and these are prone to erosion hazards. Crop cultivation- plantation crop like almond, walnut, apple, apricots etc cereals-wheat Animal domestication -goat, yak, sheep etc[cite: 14].

questions.question: Which of the following animals are majority domesticated in western Himalayan zone?
questions.explanation: Bakerwal goat is an important goat genetic resource of jammu and kashmir, reared by nomadic tribe scattered in the pir panjal himalayan mountains of south asia. The goat is scattered in hilly tracts of poonch, jammu, rajouri, udhampur and kathua of jammu and kashmir. Some common breeds reared in kashmir are gurezi, bakerwali, poonchi and karnahi sheep[cite: 14].

questions.question: Identify the major plantation crop of eastern Himalayan region
questions.explanation: Eastern himalayan zone-sikkim and darjeeling hills, arunachal pradesh, meghalaya, nagaland, manipur, tripura, mizoram, assam and jalpaiguri and cooch bihar district of west bengal fall under this region, Major crop cultivation- tea plantation, rice, maize, vegetables etc. & shifting cultivation Animal domesticated -pig, sheep, cattle ex mithun breed[cite: 14].

questions.question: ___ region is characterised by the podzolic & skeletal soil
questions.explanation: Western Himalayan zone-this zone consists of three distinct sub-zones of Jammu and Kashmir, himachal pradesh and uttar pradesh hills. Features: The region consists of skeletal soils of cold region, podzolic mountain meadow soils and hilly brown soils[cite: 14].

questions.question: This region is characterized by the high forest cover with high rainfall, small mountains, shifting cultivation is the major form of cultivation in this region identify the region
questions.explanation: Eastern himalayan zone-sikkim and darjeeling hills, arunachal pradesh, meghalaya, nagaland, manipur, tripura, mizoram, assam and jalpaiguri and cooch bihar districts of west bengal fall under this region. Features: High rainfall and high forest cover. Shifting cultivation is practiced in nearly one-third of the cultivated area and this has caused denudation and degradation of soils[cite: 14].

questions.question: Zaffran cultivation is practiced in which of the following regions?
questions.explanation: Zaffran is widely cultivated in Kashmir which lies in western Himalayan agroclimatic region[cite: 14].

questions.question: Jute is a major crop in which of the following agroclimatic region
questions.explanation: Lower Gangetic plains zone-this zone consists of west Bengal-lower Gangetic plain region. Feature: The soils are mostly alluvial and are prone to floods. Crop cultivation - rice & jute, vegetables ex cauliflower[cite: 14].

questions.question: Which of the following states lies in western Gangetic plains?

options.a: Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh hills

questions.explanation: Western himalayan zone-this zone consists of three distinct sub-zones of jammu and kashmir, himachal pradesh and uttar pradesh hills[cite: 14].

questions.question: West Bengal lies in which of the following agroclimatic regions of the country?
questions.explanation: Lower gangetic plains zone-this zone consists of west Bengal-lower Gangetic plain region[cite: 14].

questions.question: Which agroclimatic zone is highly flooded by the rivers every monsoon?
questions.explanation: Highly flooded region by ganga river system & Brahmaputra River system in the Lower Gangetic plains[cite: 14].

questions.question: Districts of Uttar Pradesh & Bihar lies in which agroclimatic zone?
questions.explanation: Middle Gangetic plains zone this zone consists of 12 districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and 27 districts of Bihar plains[cite: 14].

questions.question: This agroclimatic zone has a good potential of ground water resource and cannel & tubewells are used for irrigation purpose
questions.explanation: Upper Gangetic Plains zone: This zone consists of 32 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Irrigation is through canals and tube wells. A good potential for exploitation of ground water exists[cite: 14].

questions.question: Punjab & Haryana lies in which of the following agroclimatic zones of the country?
questions.explanation: Trans-gangetic plains zone-this zone consists of punjab, haryana, union territories of delhi and chandigarh and sri ganganagar district of rajasthan[cite: 14].

questions.question: East of Madhya Pradesh, inland Orissa & south of west Bengal lies in which of the following agroclimatic zones
questions.explanation: Eastern plateau and hills zone -this zone consists of eastern part of madhya pradesh, southern part of west bengal and most of inland orissa[cite: 14].

questions.question: This agroclimatic zone is characterized by the topography with a slope of 1 to 10%
questions.explanation: The Eastern Plateau and Hills is an agro-climatic zone in India that includes parts of Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal. Topography: Undulating with a slope of 1-10%[cite: 14].

questions.question: Which state is largest producer of cotton according to 2022-23 agricultural census?
questions.explanation: Gujrat is the largest producer of cotton in India. Cotton is one of the most important fibre crops and cash crops in India[cite: 14].

questions.question: In this region 75% area is dependent on rainfall for agriculture & grow only short duration crop or low value cereals
questions.explanation: Central plateau and hills zone-this zone comprises of 46 districts of Madhya Pradesh, part of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. 75% of the area is rainfed grown with low value cereal crops[cite: 14].

questions.question: In this agroclimatic zone dryland farming is adopted in 81% of the area and the cropping intensity is 111 percent
questions.explanation: Southern plateau and hills zone-this zone comprises 35 districts of andhra pradesh, karnataka and tamil nadu which are typically semi-arid zones. Dryland farming is adopted in 81% of the area and the cropping intensity is 111 percent[cite: 14].

questions.question: Madhya Pradesh, southern Uttar Pradesh & few districts of Rajasthan lie in which of the following agroclimatic zones of the country.
questions.explanation: Central plateau and hills zone-this zone comprises of 46 districts of Madhya Pradesh, part of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan[cite: 14].

questions.question: Agroclimatic zones have the average rainfall of 904 mm & rainfed agriculture is practiced in this region.
questions.explanation: Western plateau and hills zone-this zone comprises the major part of Maharashtra, parts of Madhya Pradesh and one district of Rajasthan. The average rainfall of the zone is 904 mm[cite: 14].

questions.question: This zone comprises of east coast of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, & Orissa.

options.a: East coast plains and hills zone

questions.explanation: This zone comprises of east coast of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Orissa. Soils are mainly alluvial and coastal sands[cite: 14].

questions.question: Cumin is the major crop in which of the following region
questions.explanation: Cumin acreage in Gujarat in 2022-23 was only 2.75 lh. The state is the largest cumin producer in India followed by Rajasthan[cite: 14].

questions.question: Cashew is a major crop of which of the following agroclimatic zone?
questions.explanation: Cashew is grown in states like Maharashtra, goa, Kerala etc which falls ion western coast & western ghat region[cite: 14].

questions.question: Kankrej draught breed of cattle is widely domesticated in which of the following agroclimatic zone?
questions.explanation: Kankrej breed has originated from kank taluka of banaskantha district, gujarat state of india[cite: 14].

questions.question: Fishery is practised in the rice field in this agroclimatic zone?
questions.explanation: Fish is widely domesticated in the rice field in Godavari basin of Andhra Pradesh region which lies in the east coast & hill agroclimatic zones of India[cite: 14].
